notes: Ruderman's question (for all p,q there is n >= 1, 2n >= p, with n!(n+q)! | (2n-p)!) is equivalent to Erdos problem 727 (for all k >= 2 infinitely many n with ((n+k)!)^2 | (2n)!) and to the existence of one such n for each k (B31_4_main, B31_4_weak in B31_4_mathlib.lean; Bertrand gives the step from one solution to infinitely many). Both stay open. Known: p <= 2 (Erdos-Graham-Ruzsa-Straus). Computed: all pairs with p + 2q <= 16, and the largest q per p <= 12 listed in the README. Outside Lean: the computed witnesses (C search plus an independent Legendre check in Python) and the known p <= 2 theorem.

sources.cite: Erdos, Graham, Ruzsa, Straus, Math. Comp. 29 (1975) 83-92

sources.what: least n for k <= 9; no prime in [a(k)+1, a(k)+k]

prior_art.note: The equivalence Ruderman <=> Erdos 727 was not found stated; its ingredients (monotonicity, prime gap after a solution) are elementary.
